Name: Windows Server Foundation Posture
Framework: Windows Server foundation posture (documented Microsoft settings)
Description: Original, limited configuration assessment for Windows Server 2019, 2022 and 2025. It is not a complete CIS, Microsoft security baseline, DISA STIG or Essential Eight assessment. Thresholds are kit policy choices. Explicit registry checks assess policy values; missing evidence remains Review. Review customer requirements and platform-specific behavior before remediation.

Controls.Title: Domain firewall profile enabled
Controls.Rationale: Host firewall profiles should remain enabled.
Controls.Remediation: Enable this profile through approved firewall policy.

Controls.Title: Domain default inbound action blocks
Controls.Rationale: Unmatched inbound connections should be blocked.
Controls.Remediation: Set the profile default inbound action to Block; review allowed rules separately.

Controls.Title: Private firewall profile enabled
Controls.Rationale: Host firewall profiles should remain enabled.
Controls.Remediation: Enable this profile through approved firewall policy.

Controls.Title: Private default inbound action blocks
Controls.Rationale: Unmatched inbound connections should be blocked.
Controls.Remediation: Set the profile default inbound action to Block; review allowed rules separately.

Controls.Title: Public firewall profile enabled
Controls.Rationale: Host firewall profiles should remain enabled.
Controls.Remediation: Enable this profile through approved firewall policy.

Controls.Title: Public default inbound action blocks
Controls.Rationale: Unmatched inbound connections should be blocked.
Controls.Remediation: Set the profile default inbound action to Block; review allowed rules separately.

Controls.Title: SMB server SMB1 protocol disabled
Controls.Rationale: Legacy SMB1 increases exposure. This checks server protocol configuration only.
Controls.Remediation: Remove legacy dependencies, then disable SMB1 through change control; separately verify the SMB1 client feature.

Controls.Title: SMB server signing required
Controls.Rationale: Require integrity protection for incoming SMB sessions.
Controls.Remediation: Require SMB server signing after validating client compatibility.

Controls.Title: SMB client signing required
Controls.Rationale: Require integrity protection for outgoing SMB sessions.
Controls.Remediation: Require SMB client signing after validating target compatibility.

Controls.Title: SMB client insecure guest authentication disabled
Controls.Rationale: Guest SMB authentication lacks normal authenticated-session protections.
Controls.Remediation: Disable insecure guest logons; replace or reconfigure guest-only storage.

Controls.Title: Defender-specific antivirus active
Controls.Rationale: This checks Defender, not the health of every possible security product.
Controls.Remediation: Enable the approved Defender configuration, or document an exception with verified alternative product evidence under WSK-106.

Controls.Title: Defender-specific real-time protection active
Controls.Rationale: Active real-time inspection is expected when Defender is the primary antivirus.
Controls.Remediation: Restore Defender real-time protection or document the approved alternative-product design and health evidence.

Controls.Title: Defender security intelligence age within kit threshold
Controls.Rationale: This kit uses a one-day freshness threshold; it does not prove malware detection or EDR coverage.
Controls.Remediation: Investigate intelligence update delivery. If Defender is intentionally passive, assess the approved primary product and record an exception.

Controls.Title: OS volume fully encrypted with BitLocker protection enabled
Controls.Rationale: This checks both active protection and completed OS-volume encryption; it does not validate recovery escrow, other volumes, or storage-platform encryption.
Controls.Remediation: Plan OS-volume protection and recovery testing; confirm encryption completes and protection is not suspended. For an approved alternative encryption design, retain architecture and key-management evidence.

Controls.Title: Local-account minimum password length meets kit threshold
Controls.Rationale: A local merged-policy value is a configuration observation, not proof of all users password strength.
Controls.Remediation: Set a tested local-account minimum length of at least 14, or use an approved customer profile. Assess domain accounts separately.

Controls.Title: Local-account password complexity policy enabled
Controls.Rationale: Complexity policy is checked only for the local account policy.
Controls.Remediation: Enable complexity in the approved local-account policy; validate actual identity controls separately.

Controls.Title: Local-account password history retains 24 passwords
Controls.Rationale: Password history limits reuse; password-age policy and managed-account design also affect effectiveness.
Controls.Remediation: Configure local password history to 24 and review minimum age alongside account-management requirements.

Controls.Title: Local-account lockout threshold is bounded
Controls.Rationale: A nonzero threshold limits repeated guessing. Very low thresholds can create denial-of-service risk.
Controls.Remediation: Use the approved local lockout policy; 10 attempts is a starting point. Validate duration, reset interval and operational impact together.

Controls.Title: Local-account lockout counter reset meets kit interval
Controls.Rationale: This checks the reset interval alone; a passing value does not establish that lockout is enabled.
Controls.Remediation: Review with WSK-018 and the effective lockout duration. Select a tested reset interval and document customer-specific exceptions.

Controls.Title: Local reversible-password storage policy disabled
Controls.Rationale: Reversible storage increases credential exposure. Policy state does not prove existing passwords were replaced.
Controls.Remediation: Disable reversible storage after removing dependencies; follow the approved process to replace affected credentials.

Controls.Title: UAC Admin Approval Mode policy enabled
Controls.Rationale: UAC policy should remain enabled. A pending restart can affect current enforcement.
Controls.Remediation: Enable UAC in the approved security policy and complete any required restart.

Controls.Title: UAC administrator prompt policy uses secure options
Controls.Rationale: The kit accepts secure-desktop credentials, consent, or consent for non-Windows binaries.
Controls.Remediation: Select an accepted administrator prompt policy and retain secure-desktop prompting.

Controls.Title: UAC standard-user elevation policy denies requests
Controls.Rationale: This foundation profile expects administrative work to use a separate approved path.
Controls.Remediation: Set standard-user elevation requests to automatic denial, or document a tested credential-prompt exception.

Controls.Title: UAC secure-desktop prompt policy enabled
Controls.Rationale: Secure-desktop prompting helps protect the elevation interaction.
Controls.Remediation: Enable secure-desktop prompting in the approved UAC policy.

Controls.Title: Legacy LM hash creation policy disabled
Controls.Rationale: This legacy setting prevents new LM hash storage; existing credential history needs separate review.
Controls.Remediation: Enable the policy against LM hash storage and review credential rotation. This policy is excluded on Server 2025.

Controls.Title: Legacy LAN Manager policy requires NTLMv2
Controls.Rationale: For 2019/2022, this is an explicit legacy-authentication policy check, not an audit of all authentication traffic.
Controls.Remediation: Test legacy dependencies, then configure NTLMv2-only responses with LM and NTLM refusal. Prefer Kerberos and assess remaining NTLM use.

Controls.Title: WDigest credential-caching policy explicitly disabled
Controls.Rationale: Checks explicit configuration only. A missing value may inherit a secure default but remains Review in this kit.
Controls.Remediation: Confirm the effective configuration and supported OS behavior; enforce the approved explicit value when appropriate.

Controls.Title: Windows PowerShell script-block logging policy enabled
Controls.Rationale: This checks Windows PowerShell policy, not log delivery, retention, PowerShell 7, or successful recording.
Controls.Remediation: Enable script-block logging with protected event handling and validate collection; logs can contain sensitive script data.

Controls.Title: Machine inactivity limit within kit range
Controls.Rationale: The kit expects an explicit inactivity timeout; this is not a complete RDP-session policy assessment.
Controls.Remediation: Set a tested inactivity limit of at most 15 minutes and validate the actual session-lock behavior.

Controls.Title: Machine Windows Installer elevated-install policy disabled
Controls.Rationale: This checks the machine policy only. Users can configure their own corresponding value when machine policy permits elevation.
Controls.Remediation: Disable the machine elevated-install policy and review user-side policy as part of deployment hardening.

Controls.Title: Advanced audit-policy override explicitly enabled
Controls.Rationale: This checks policy precedence, not which audit subcategories are enabled or whether events reach the SIEM.
Controls.Remediation: Enable subcategory-policy precedence, then separately validate effective auditpol output, retention and event forwarding.

Controls.Title: LLMNR policy explicitly disabled
Controls.Rationale: This checks multicast name-resolution policy; DNS and application name-resolution behavior need separate testing.
Controls.Remediation: Disable LLMNR through the DNS Client policy after validating DNS and dependent application resolution.

Controls.Title: Verify MFA and privileged access coverage
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Reviewed access paths, MFA enforcement and privileged-access evidence
Controls.Rationale: A local scan cannot establish MFA coverage or appropriate administrator membership.
Controls.Remediation: Review admin accounts, remote-management paths, MFA enforcement, service identities and periodic access reviews. Retain customer-approved evidence.

Controls.Title: Verify backup protection and successful recovery
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Recent restore evidence and approved backup protection
Controls.Rationale: Successful local commands do not prove recoverability.
Controls.Remediation: Review backup isolation, access separation, retention and representative restore tests against the agreed recovery objectives.

Controls.Title: Verify OS and application vulnerability remediation
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Authoritative inventory and vulnerability/patch SLA evidence
Controls.Rationale: Installed-hotfix dates alone do not establish current vulnerability exposure.
Controls.Remediation: Use the approved patch/vulnerability platform to verify OS and application coverage, missing updates, maintenance windows and overdue exceptions.

Controls.Title: Verify enforced application control
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Enforced policy with application coverage and bypass testing
Controls.Rationale: Policy presence alone does not establish effective application control.
Controls.Remediation: Review application-control policy mode, scope, approved software, enforcement events and controlled validation results.

Controls.Title: Verify effective domain identity and password policies
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Domain policy, resultant fine-grained policy and privileged-account review
Controls.Rationale: Local merged security-policy values do not establish domain account or fine-grained password policy.
Controls.Remediation: Review default domain policy, password settings objects and resultant policies for representative accounts; validate lockout, service accounts and privileged access.

Controls.Title: Verify approved antivirus and EDR product health
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Primary product, reporting freshness and monitored alert evidence
Controls.Rationale: Defender may be intentionally passive or replaced. A Defender finding is not proof that all endpoint protection is absent.
Controls.Remediation: Confirm the approved primary product and EDR coverage in their management consoles, including last check-in, tamper protection and alert routing; document justified Defender exceptions.

Controls.Title: Verify DC LDAP signing and channel binding
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Role/version-aware effective policy, compatibility and connection evidence
Controls.Rationale: LDAP defaults and enforcement precedence differ across releases and new versus upgraded deployments.
Controls.Remediation: Review effective signing enforcement and channel binding together with client compatibility and Directory Service audit events. Validate the approved policy before enforcing changes.

Controls.Title: Verify remote access and TLS exposure
Controls.ExpectedDisplay: Approved listeners, NLA/TLS settings, certificates and network restrictions
Controls.Rationale: One registry value cannot establish the security of all RDP, WinRM, IIS or application listeners.
Controls.Remediation: Inventory required listeners; validate RDP NLA where enabled, secure transport, certificates, network restrictions and the absence of unnecessary exposed services.
